theme: Reading the rest of the file after a syntax error
title: Cascading Recovery: Context-Aware Panic-Mode Synchronization
innovation_hook: Skipping to the next semicolon recovers fast but produces phantom cascades or suppressed errors; the insight is choosing synchronization tokens by which enclosing construct (statement / paren-group / for-header) is still open on the parse stack, not a single fixed token set.
strategies: empty-everywhere: give up after the first error in each program (reproduces the checker baseline B -> ~0.1)

fixed always-resync-to-`;`: fast and fine for isolated statement-level errors, but inside a paren group or for-header it either swallows a sibling opening bracket (later phantom mismatch) or swallows a second nearby error (suppression)
context-aware table (statement:`; }`, paren:`, )`, for-header:`; )`): each construct's own terminator is found first, so it neither over-skips nor cascades
